date: "2026-09-28"
---

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# FIGURE 5 — REVISED STANDALONE SCRIPT
#
# A. Pairwise 5' LTR identity for the 17 largest expressed 5' LTR families
#    using the EXISTING within-expression-cluster VSEARCH comparisons.
# B. Pairwise 5' LTR identity within the 17 expression clusters.
# C. Number of 5' LTR families represented per expression cluster.
# D. Number of expression clusters occupied per 5' LTR family.
#
# NOTE FOR PANEL A:
# This intentionally reuses the old working pairwise analysis. Therefore,
# Panel A includes same-family pairs that were compared within an expression
# cluster; it does not generate new across-cluster pairwise comparisons.
# ==============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(purrr)
  library(stringr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
  library(scales)
})

analysis_dir <-
  "/projects/standard/hirschc1/menar060/family_analysis/expression_cluster_sequence_identity/figures"

vsearch_dir <-
  "/projects/standard/hirschc1/menar060/family_analysis/expression_cluster_sequence_identity/vsearch"

fiveprime_silix_path <-
  "/projects/standard/hirschc1/menar060/family_analysis/redo_five_prime/B73/output/B73_five_prime_silix.out"

output_dir <- "/users/2/menar060/final_panel_figures"
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOAD THE SAME SAVED TABLES USED BY THE OLD WORKING FIGURE
# ==============================================================================

panelC_path <- file.path(
  analysis_dir,
  "PanelA_5prime_families_per_expression_cluster.tsv"
)

panelD_candidates <- c(
  file.path(analysis_dir, "PanelB_expression_clusters_per_5prime_family.tsv"),
  file.path(analysis_dir, "PanelB_expression_cluster_occupancy_distribution.tsv"),
  file.path(analysis_dir, "PanelD_family_size_vs_expression_cluster_occupancy.tsv")
)

panelD_path <- panelD_candidates[file.exists(panelD_candidates)][1]

if (!file.exists(panelC_path)) {
  stop("Missing old Panel A data: ", panelC_path)
}
if (length(panelD_path) == 0 || is.na(panelD_path)) {
  stop("Could not find the saved family-level occupancy table.")
}
if (!file.exists(fiveprime_silix_path)) {
  stop("Missing 5' LTR SiLiX output: ", fiveprime_silix_path)
}

panelC_data <- readr::read_tsv(panelC_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
family_level_data <- readr::read_tsv(panelD_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. READ THE EXISTING 17 EXPRESSION-CLUSTER VSEARCH FILES
# ==============================================================================

vsearch_files <- list.files(
  vsearch_dir,
  pattern = "^cluster_[0-9]+_5prime_allpairs\\.tsv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

if (length(vsearch_files) != 17) {
  stop(
    "Expected 17 existing VSEARCH files but found ",
    length(vsearch_files),
    " in ",
    vsearch_dir
  )
}

blast6_columns <- c(
  "Query", "Target", "Percent_Identity", "Alignment_Length",
  "Mismatches", "Gap_Opens", "Query_Start", "Query_End",
  "Target_Start", "Target_End", "Evalue", "Bit_Score"
)

read_cluster_vsearch <- function(file) {
  cluster_number <- basename(file) %>%
    stringr::str_extract("(?<=cluster_)\\d+") %>%
    as.integer()

  readr::read_tsv(
    file,
    col_names = blast6_columns,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Expression_Cluster = cluster_number, .before = 1)
}

pairwise_raw <- purrr::map_dfr(vsearch_files, read_cluster_vsearch)

# Clean IDs and collapse reciprocal pairs within each expression cluster.
pairwise_identity <- pairwise_raw %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Query_lLTR_ID = stringr::str_extract(Query, "lLTR_[0-9]+"),
    Target_lLTR_ID = stringr::str_extract(Target, "lLTR_[0-9]+")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Query_lLTR_ID),
    !is.na(Target_lLTR_ID),
    Query_lLTR_ID != Target_lLTR_ID,
    !is.na(Percent_Identity)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Pair_1 = pmin(Query_lLTR_ID, Target_lLTR_ID),
    Pair_2 = pmax(Query_lLTR_ID, Target_lLTR_ID)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    Expression_Cluster,
    Pair_1,
    Pair_2,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 3. CORRECTLY PARSE THE EXISTING SiLiX FAMILY ASSIGNMENTS
# ==============================================================================

silix_raw <- readr::read_tsv(
  fiveprime_silix_path,
  col_names = c("Five_Prime_Family_ID", "Attributes"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

fiveprime_lookup <- silix_raw %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    lLTR_ID = sub("^ID=([^;]+);.*$", "\\1", Attributes)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(lLTR_ID, Five_Prime_Family_ID) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(lLTR_ID), !is.na(Five_Prime_Family_ID)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

# Map both members of every existing pair to their 5' LTR family.
pairwise_with_families <- pairwise_identity %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    fiveprime_lookup %>%
      dplyr::rename(
        Query_lLTR_ID = lLTR_ID,
        Query_5prime_Family = Five_Prime_Family_ID
      ),
    by = "Query_lLTR_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    fiveprime_lookup %>%
      dplyr::rename(
        Target_lLTR_ID = lLTR_ID,
        Target_5prime_Family = Five_Prime_Family_ID
      ),
    by = "Target_lLTR_ID"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 4. IDENTIFY THE 17 LARGEST EXPRESSED 5' LTR FAMILIES
# ==============================================================================

# Prefer the saved family-level table because it already contains Number_TEs.
if (all(c("Five_Prime_Family", "Number_TEs") %in% names(family_level_data))) {

  top17_families <- family_level_data %>%
    dplyr::select(Five_Prime_Family, Number_TEs) %>%
    dplyr::distinct() %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Number_TEs), Five_Prime_Family) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 17)

} else {

  # Fallback: count unique lLTR IDs represented in the existing pairwise data.
  expressed_family_members <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    pairwise_with_families %>%
      dplyr::transmute(
        lLTR_ID = Query_lLTR_ID,
        Five_Prime_Family = Query_5prime_Family
      ),
    pairwise_with_families %>%
      dplyr::transmute(
        lLTR_ID = Target_lLTR_ID,
        Five_Prime_Family = Target_5prime_Family
      )
  ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Five_Prime_Family)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct()

  top17_families <- expressed_family_members %>%
    dplyr::count(Five_Prime_Family, name = "Number_TEs") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Number_TEs), Five_Prime_Family) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 17)
}

cat("\n17 largest expressed 5' LTR families:\n")
print(top17_families, n = Inf)

# ==============================================================================
# 5. NEW PANEL A
# SAME-FAMILY PAIRWISE IDENTITY FOR THE TOP 17 FAMILIES
# ==============================================================================

panelA_data <- pairwise_with_families %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Query_5prime_Family),
    !is.na(Target_5prime_Family),
    Query_5prime_Family == Target_5prime_Family,
    Query_5prime_Family %in% top17_families$Five_Prime_Family
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Five_Prime_Family = Query_5prime_Family,
    Percent_Identity
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(top17_families, by = "Five_Prime_Family") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Five_Prime_Family = factor(
      Five_Prime_Family,
      levels = top17_families$Five_Prime_Family
    )
  )

if (nrow(panelA_data) == 0) {
  stop(
    "Panel A is empty after family matching. ",
    "Inspect the SiLiX ID parsing and family names."
  )
}

cat("\nPanel A families with pairwise comparisons: ",
    dplyr::n_distinct(panelA_data$Five_Prime_Family), "\n", sep = "")

print(
  panelA_data %>%
    dplyr::count(Five_Prime_Family, Number_TEs, name = "Number_Pairs"),
  n = Inf
)

pA <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  panelA_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Five_Prime_Family,
    y = Percent_Identity
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.70,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    linewidth = 0.45,
    fill = "grey40"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 80,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(35, 100),
    breaks = c(40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "5' LTR family",
    y = "Pairwise 5' LTR\nsequence identity (%)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 7.5
    )
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 6. PANEL B
# PAIRWISE IDENTITY WITHIN EACH EXPRESSION CLUSTER
# ==============================================================================

panelB_data <- pairwise_identity %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Expression_Cluster = factor(
      Expression_Cluster,
      levels = 1:17
    )
  )

pB <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  panelB_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Expression_Cluster,
    y = Percent_Identity
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.70,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    linewidth = 0.45,
    fill = "grey55"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 80,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(35, 100),
    breaks = c(40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Expression cluster",
    y = "Pairwise 5' LTR\nsequence identity (%)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 7. PANEL C — OLD PANEL A
# ==============================================================================

panelC_data <- panelC_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Expression_Cluster = factor(
      as.character(Expression_Cluster),
      levels = as.character(1:17)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Expression_Cluster)

pC <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  panelC_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Expression_Cluster,
    y = Number_5prime_Families
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.75, fill = "grey40") +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = Number_5prime_Families),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Expression cluster",
    y = "5' LTR families\nper expression cluster"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 8. PANEL D — OLD PANEL B
# ==============================================================================

if (all(
  c("Number_Expression_Clusters", "Number_5prime_Families") %in%
    names(family_level_data)
)) {

  panelD_data <- family_level_data %>%
    dplyr::select(Number_Expression_Clusters, Number_5prime_Families) %>%
    dplyr::distinct()

} else if (all(
  c("Number_Expression_Clusters", "Five_Prime_Family") %in%
    names(family_level_data)
)) {

  panelD_data <- family_level_data %>%
    dplyr::count(
      Number_Expression_Clusters,
      name = "Number_5prime_Families"
    )

} else {
  stop("Could not construct Panel D from the saved family-level table.")
}

panelD_data <- panelD_data %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    Number_Expression_Clusters = 1:17,
    fill = list(Number_5prime_Families = 0)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Number_Expression_Clusters)

total_5prime_families <- sum(panelD_data$Number_5prime_Families)

one_cluster_families <- panelD_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(Number_Expression_Clusters == 1) %>%
  dplyr::pull(Number_5prime_Families)

percent_one_cluster <- 100 * one_cluster_families / total_5prime_families

pD <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  panelD_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = factor(Number_Expression_Clusters, levels = 1:17),
    y = Number_5prime_Families
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.75, fill = "grey40") +
  # Label only the first (single-cluster) bar.
  # Shift the label to the right so it does not collide with the y-axis.
  ggplot2::annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1.65,
    # Keep the label comfortably below the top of the panel.
    y = one_cluster_families +
      0.025 * max(panelD_data$Number_5prime_Families),
    label = paste0(
      scales::comma(one_cluster_families),
      " families\n(",
      round(percent_one_cluster, 1),
      "%)"
    ),
    hjust = 0,
    vjust = 0,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.4
  ) +
  # Fix Panel D y-axis at 0–2,000 so the first-bar label has ample room.
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 2000),
    breaks = c(0, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000),
    labels = scales::comma,
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Expression clusters occupied",
    y = "Number of\n5' LTR families"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 9. COMBINE
# ==============================================================================

figure5_final <- (pA | pB) / (pC | pD) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1), heights = c(1, 1)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "A"
  ) &
  ggplot2::theme(
    # Apply directly to every panel tag in the completed patchwork.
    plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 19
    ),
    plot.tag.position = c(0.01, 0.99)
  )

print(figure5_final)

# ==============================================================================
# 10. SAVE
# ==============================================================================

ggplot2::ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "Figure5_FINAL.jpeg"),
  figure5_final,
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "Figure5_FINAL.pdf"),
  figure5_final,
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  units = "in",
  bg = "white"
)

# Save the new Panel A data so it can be inspected directly.
readr::write_tsv(
  panelA_data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Five_Prime_Family = as.character(Five_Prime_Family)
    ),
  file.path(output_dir, "Figure5_PanelA_top17_family_identity.tsv")
)

readr::write_tsv(
  top17_families,
  file.path(output_dir, "Figure5_top17_expressed_5prime_families.tsv")
)

cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "FIGURE 5 COMPLETE\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  "Panel A families plotted: ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(panelA_data$Five_Prime_Family),
  "\nPanel B expression clusters plotted: ",
  dplyr::n_distinct(panelB_data$Expression_Cluster),
  "\nPanel D one-cluster families: ",
  one_cluster_families,
  " / ",
  total_5prime_families,
  " (",
  round(percent_one_cluster, 1),
  "%)\n",
  "Output directory: ",
  output_dir,
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

```
